answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A comet delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A timber check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A ember penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 10404 identities need 10404 bonds of 45 tokens, 6016 dollars of hardware and 44 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
